Well with one sec you have to wait the full 5 minutes INSIDE the app to be able to use it again, or you’ll have to wait for the timeout to expire every, single time you reopen the app. Only way to fix this? get pro which is stupid 

The last straw was when the stupid intervention feature wasn’t working properly at all. I needed to use YouTube for an emergency but every time I went through the intervention YouTube was still blocked. Don’t make so many features paid if the basic ones aren’t even working properly.

reviews.title: Changed my life! Would recommend one big change though
reviews.text:
I LOVE one sec! I've been using it for at least a couple of years now. The combination of using One Sec and deleting the instagram app has basically changed my life. The best features are: 
1. Being able to set time frame blocks for certain apps and websites (so helpful for not scrolling during work hours or late at night!)
2. Being able to set a timer for how many minutes you'd like to spend in the app before another intervention
3. Just making my distracting apps and websites less of a favorable activity (aka more annoying bc I keep getting interrupted!)

I would only make one big change to improve this app. Let's use Facebook for example. When you click on Facebook, it immediately runs OneSec and starts an animation such as the screen going dark for several seconds. This is designed to slow you down and help you consider clearly whether you actually want to be opening that app right now. It's meant to prevent mindlessly opening up apps. When the animation is finished,  it asks you if you really want to open facebook. Well, you've already waited the several seconds for the animation- you may as well open it! You open facebook. 

If onesec asked me if I wanted to open it BEFORE the intervention animation started, that would be a game changer. That way it would be a trade: you have to pay to open this app- you can only open it if you wait several boring seconds first. Then if you click yes to continue to the intervention, and then the intervention finishes, it still asks you what your reason for opening the app is and how many minutes you want to spend on there before another intervention. 

Mane this could be a setting you ca toggle on and off, so if anyone doesn't like that system they can opt out. THEN the app would be perfect. What do we think?

reviews.title: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability
reviews.text:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.

You can also set up a bedtime schedule where it blocks all apps and websites. It provides an informative dashboard detailing approximately how much time you saved. However, I really can’t get behind the modern era of subscription based apps. Especially for the lifetime license costing a whopping FIFTY dollars, and SEVENTY for a “family plan”. I don’t have any problem supporting independent developers and paying for software, but I personally feel like this is overpriced for what it does. Most of it is just relying on the iOS shortcuts functionality anyway, and all the app is doing is showing a pretty GUI and recording the time. You could replicate something similar in shortcuts (although not entirely, like website blocking for instance.) If you don’t mind the cost, go for it, but I would probably pay $15 maximum for a lifetime license, not $50. Especially considering many people using this are likely college students.

I did notice that the FAQ link in the email directs to tutorials, not a traditional FAQ - and that was my “give-up” point. reviews.title: A great app that shows great promise
reviews.text:
I’m a student who has been struggling with procrastination for as long as I can remember. My phone, through social media and video games, has often been my source of that. I’ve tried other screen time apps in a desperate attempt to fix my problem, but all of them are easy to bypass and default back to wasting time. I was afraid that I would never be able to break the cycle. 

One Sec is the only program that forces you to reflect. And I mean, really, it forces you to reflect on yourself before you open the app that you designed. There’s nothing fancy about it - no bells and whistles like the other apps. That’s because change doesn’t come with bells and whistles, it comes from within. I’ve been using One Sec for only a day and I’ve managed to drop my average screen time about an hour and a half. It’s incredible, and I’m really giddy about how much I’ve been able to improve myself in only a day.

That being said, the downside of One Sec is that it doesn’t have any bells and whistles. You have to manually implement the shortcuts for all of the apps you want to block, and that is the meat and potatoes of this app - you don’t get much else that significantly helps you stop overusing apps. On top of that, the dashboard (overview) page of the app has very little content besides the list of apps that you blocked by hand and how much time you’ve saved through using One Sec (which seems inaccurate as I tend to spend a lot more time than three minutes every time I clicked on an app). 

But overall, this app is a great program that can help you beat overuse. More content and programs are sure to come as this app is just beginning, and I really look forward to it. I think that there are a lot of great things that can happen with this app, such as more content being added to the overview page (overall screen time, usage trend graphs, times you’ve continued to use the app despite the One Sec timer, etc) and making it easier to block apps. I’m very happy with One Sec and would recommend it to anyone looking to make a change for the better.

reviews.title: What Screen Time should be.
reviews.text:
The barebones version of this app is more than enough to genuinely make an impact on your screen time. Apple's integrated Screen Time feature isn't a realistic way to rework our additions to certain apps. The one minute feature often times isnt enough, and the 15 minute feature allows you to get sucked back into the content, putting you in an endless loop of "remind me in 15 minutes" until it's been hours. One Sec not only forces you to take a moment to make sure that you truly should be using the app, but with the free re-intervention feature, it's far more effective than Apple's own Screen Time. 

I can't recommend this app enough. It is truly made with people in mind, and the free features are more than enough to make a tangible difference in your life.

reviews.text:
I’m so annoyed. I was really hoping I could use this app to curb my spending. Unfortunately, it’s useless at best and infuriating to use at worst.

Not only are the directions to set up blocking for websites basically useless (I had to Google and find answers on Reddit to figure out how to actually add websites to one sec’s block list), they also don’t even work. Even if you enable the one sec safari extension, somehow figure out you’re supposed to go to each individual website and tap on the extension button to block that website, and manage to create a block list, it simply will not work.

One sec blocked only one website for me, and the button it presented me to go back to the one sec app did not work. So I was not able to complete the breathing exercise. The app didn’t even recognize that it had blocked the website. Simply refreshing the website let me back in. After that, the blocking didn’t work at all, for that or for any website that I had put on my block list. What on earth is the point of a blocking app that doesn’t actually block anything?

Thank god I canceled before my free trial was up. It would have been a huge waste of my money on a useless app that does nothing when it comes to one of its most advertised features. If you’re looking to block websites, this app is basically a scam (because blocking websites is a premium-only feature). Stay away. I wish I could give zero stars.

Until suddenly it was telling me that “You cannot use [app name] because it is restricted.” Keep in mind that I ONLY have interventions set up for three apps from midnight-8:00am. 

Didn’t matter what time of day/night, I could not access ANY of those three apps. I managed to somehow figure out a fix for one, but for the life of me could not get it to work for the others. I turned off every thing I could find, eventually had to just completely delete the app as I needed access to event info ASAP.

It even inspired me to purchase my cousin an iPhone, knowing that I would be able to restrict their screen time and break the dopamine-induced doom scrolling that social media and games can oftentimes induce. When I was going to sign up for the family plan, I saw the price had increased from $25 to $40. For reference, the individual plan is $20. Honestly, if I only intended to add one additional user to the subscription, what incentive is there in not receiving a discount? Look at it this way: 2x individual plans = $40; 2x users on family plan = $40. What's the difference? This is really shortsighted and selfish of the developer, in my opinion, and it makes me want to not even renew the individual subscription. $40 is too much. The app is good and well thought out, but it isn't actually providing that grand of a solution to justify that price, even for multiple users. $25 actually motivated me to add users to the app, given it was only a $5 increase from what I was paying. Doubling the price only frustrates me and makes me want to protest the developer's greed, and it shows that their intent isn't to actually provide a solution and make that accessible to more people, but to squeeze every dollar from their user base. What a careless decision towards users. I'll be deleting the app.

reviews.title: Brilliant

This app is brilliant. I have it on all my iOS devices. I feel like most screen time reducing apps come and go, as half baked ideas put together over a weekend. This one is different. It feels as put together, or even more so, than Apple’s own screen time controls. It’s obvious the creator of this app made this for themselves as it applies to users’ real uses very well. I’m someone who uses various ways to make my devices more “dumb” or minimal. I mix this with feed blockers, screen time settings, greyscale, and not having social media apps on my phone. This is a very important piece of my already pretty elaborate puzzle.

This app can probably do more than I can grasp right now. I just use it to slow load apps and make them get progressively slower overtime. As my dopamine rush gets slower every time I wait for an app to load, I could just delete this app out of frustration. But I don’t. I feel like a kid knowing maybe it’s best if only mom can open the cookie jar. I also use the app for app blocking which is super cool. 

My only request is if I could set a timer for app blocking. What I mean: set timer and in 25 minutes all apps on the list will be blocked. That way maybe when I need or want to go down the rabbit hole, there is going to be a hard cutoff upcoming that I can’t stop. Otherwise I’ll just willingly not stop and go down a binge, which I unfortunately too often do.

reviews.title: Lifesaver of a time-saver
reviews.text:
I’ve been trying a few things to make my phone more annoying to use, or helpful when I do, and not a boredom eraser. One Sec is something that I wish I had years ago. I finally feel like I have the opportunity to fill my downtime with something other than my phone screen! My adhd makes all of this harder than it might otherwise be, but with a little help from this app (and a lot of work on myself), I’ve started journaling, meditating, budgeting better, doing more real-world projects around the house… the Structured integration helps with that too. By the way, I’m not sure why people are complaining about the price. $20 for a whole year is practically nothing.

Something I’d like to be able to do with the app is set a time limit on how long you can use a particular app before the interventions start. That way (if I’m good) I don’t have to wait for the intervention while I’m out at the store and trying to look something up before buying it, for example.

reviews.title: $15/year is the best investment in yourself money can buy
reviews.text:
The developers of this app deserve a Nobel Prize.

I am so grateful for one sec. You will gain full WEEKS of your life back. I had a week where I disabled one sec, I was noticeably much more depressed. When I’m using one sec I’m much happier, more productive, and doing things I put off before. We don’t even realize how much social media use is completely mindless, and you don’t miss it when it’s gone. 

“One day we’ll view Meta Technologies like Big Tobacco”
